sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Subtitle Transcription and AI Voice Cloning Studio

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU bilateral investment treaties with over 40 jurisdictions, including BLEU–China (2005), BLEU–Hong Kong (1998), BLEU–India (1997), BLEU–Argentina (1991)

Comprehensive tax treaties (DTAAs) with more than 80 jurisdictions, including Luxembourg–United States (1996/2009), Luxembourg–Germany (2012/2015), Luxembourg–France (2018/2021), Luxembourg–China (1995/2010)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement BEPS (MLI), applicable to covered Luxembourg tax agreements
EU internal market freedoms, including Article 49 TFEU (freedom of establishment)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML Law); Law of 13 January 2019 on the register of beneficial owners (RBE Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 January 2021 on AML/CFT; CSSF Regulation No. 20-01 of 28 January 2020; Luxembourg Criminal Code articles on money laundering and terrorist financing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authorities of the UBO's country of residence (passport office or civil registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (certified true copy by a notary; if the issuing country is not a Hague member, consular legalization is required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, bank statement, or government-issued attestation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, credit institution, or local municipal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague countries, consular legalization, combined with a notarized translation into English, French, or German

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, commercial register excerpt, and certificate of good standing of the corporate General Partner (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade and Companies Register / companies registry of the General Partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg registered agent / fiduciary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the grantor's jurisdiction or Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the primary banking relationship of the founders (if available)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial attestation or Hague Apostille as required by the receiving bank; otherwise direct bank confirmation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, General Partners, authorised persons and named signatories are screened pre-filing and continuously thereafter against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulations on restrictive measures), UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN list, Luxembourg domestic administrative sanctions registers, and adverse media/PEP databases. In accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Circular 20/735, enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates; the complete AML/CFT file must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), accessible via the LBR online service at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must use Latin-1 characters and include the legal form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Roman characters for registration. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names, must not be misleading, and must comply with Luxembourg public policy and official naming rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official rejection of a proposed name, the notary or legal representative may: (1) request a written reasoned refusal from the RCS; (2) file a recours gracieux (administrative appeal) with the Minister of Justice or the competent administrative authority within one month of the refusal; (3) if the administrative appeal is denied or not answered within one month, bring an application for annulment before the Tribunal administratif within three months of the decision or expiry of the one-month response period. A new name may be filed at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Generally permissible for an SCSp provided a real Luxembourg registered office address is maintained through a licensed domiciliation agent. A purely virtual office without local substance may be challenged by the tax administration or AML obliged entities during bank account opening and payment-rail onboarding; therefore the entity should maintain a service agreement with a licensed fiduciary and, if appropriate, a tax representation arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated 2–3% annual probability for a non-licensed, standard low-risk entity; probability increases to 15–20% upon negative media coverage, UBO sanctions listings, or repeated bank account denials.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and reservation filing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 101-1 to 101-24 (société en commandite spéciale, as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 30 May 2000 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, as amended; Law of 26 July 2017 on fully electronic RCS filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating under the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Single electronic application for registration (demande d'immatriculation) filed via the LBR eFile portal, accompanied by the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) signed in writing or by LuxTrust electronic signature; the registered extract is then published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. An SCSp has no statutory minimum capital and no legal capital requirement; the partnership agreement freely defines the capital and the contributions of the General Partner and the Limited Partners. Cash contributions require no escrow or blocked account: the subscribed amount is paid into the SCSp's account and evidenced by a bank confirmation; in-kind contributions are described and valued in the agreement. The SCSp is fiscally transparent (pass-through), so Luxembourg taxation occurs at partner level.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The company, acting as General Partner of the SCSp, approves the partnership agreement dated [DATE] and subscribes to the capital contribution allocated. (2) The registered office of the SCSp is established at 12 Rue de l'Église, L-1458 Luxembourg. (3) [NAME] is appointed manager with sole signature, authorised to open the bank account, maintain registers and complete all filings. (4) The manager is directed to file the SCSp with the RCS via eFile, arrange the RESA publication, and apply for the business permit, VAT number, and employer registration. (5) All acts of the founders before this resolution are ratified. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement and contribution statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private parties; for an SCSp a written agreement (signed by all partners) suffices; electronic signature via LuxTrust is valid. If real estate is contributed, the deed must be executed before a Luxembourg notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement containing the exact corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate purpose limited to ISIC 5912 (audio post-production, AI subtitle transcription and voice services), duration, capital and contributions, identity and signatures of the General Partner and all Limited Partners, profit-sharing, management and representation rules, transfer restrictions, and dissolution terms. Verify name availability against the RCS index; obtain the registered office occupancy title or a domiciliation acceptance letter; each partner provides identification and evidence of signature capacity.
required_dossiers: Duly executed partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Passport or national ID copies of all partners
Written power of attorney of any signatory proxy
Cash contribution statement or valuation report for in-kind contributions
Proof of registered office address (lease, ownership title, or domiciliation service agreement)
Name availability verification from the RCS index
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or a notary identifies omissions (e.g., missing purpose, capital clause, or erroneous partner identification), execute a corrective addendum or re-sign the corrected agreement; notarial authentication becomes mandatory if the SCSp acquires real property; all corrections must be completed within one month of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation application with the RCS through the eFile portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing service (eFile).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account on the LBR eFile platform and complete the electronic application for registration ('demande d'immatriculation'): state the exact entity name, legal form 'SCSp', registered office address, corporate object (NACE code 59.12), duration, details of the General Partner and manager(s), and the absence of a legal capital threshold. Upload the executed partnership agreement and the supporting dossiers, sign electronically with LuxTrust certificates, and pay the EUR 24 filing fee online. Track the dossier status and respond to any LBR queries within the stated deadline.
required_dossiers: Completed eFile registration application
Executed partnership agreement (PDF)
LuxTrust certificates and identity documents of the General Partner's governing persons
Consent forms and specimen signatures of the appointed manager
Proof of registered office address
Payment confirmation of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The RCS may issue a 'demande de régularisation' (query) listing defects or missing documents; the filer must respond within 15 days with corrected documents or a new electronic signature. Failure to cure results in closure of the file and loss of fees; a fresh application must then be submitted with a new payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory extract in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations), publication service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically forwards the registration extract (date of constitution, legal form, name, registered office, identity of the General Partner, capital and managers) to the RESA. Verify the published notice on the official RESA website within the statutory one-month publication window. The publication fee of EUR 50 is collected by LBR and covers the official third-party notice of the SCSp's existence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate or extract
Publication notice generated by the RCS
Proof of payment of the RESA publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published RESA notice contains errors (name, address, manager), submit a rectification request to the RCS accompanied by the registrar's certificate and pay the rectification fee; the erroneous notice is cured by a corrected publication at the entity's cost. Any delay is remedied by a same-day supplementary filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the business establishment authorization and employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de l'industrie et de la compétitivité; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) for employer affiliation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online through MyGuichet.lu for the 'autorisation d'établissement' (business establishment permit) for the activity of video and audio post-production (NACE 59.12). The permit is issued to the SCSp on condition that the natural person entrusted with management holds the required professional qualification (diploma or three years of documented professional experience in the sector) and provides a clean criminal record. Upon approval, and before the first hire, register the SCSp with the CCSS to obtain the employer matricule number; affiliation is completed via the Edital or CCSS online forms.
required_dossiers: Completed MyGuichet application for autorisation d'établissement
RCS extract showing the SCSp registration
Proof of professional qualification of the managing person
Certificate of good conduct (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the managing person
Identity and residence permit of the managing person
Occupancy title and commune building permits for the studio premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry refuses the permit, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal within three months; if the file is incomplete, respond to the 'complément' notice within the prescribed period, and where the manager lacks qualification, appoint a qualified director and re-submit. A new application may be filed after a three-month cooling-off period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Registration Office; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg income tax office; commune of the registered office for municipal business tax.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS extract and the business establishment permit, submit the VAT registration application to the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number under the Law of 12 February 1979. Register the SCSp with the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, and confirm the tax-transparent (pass-through) status of the SCSp so that profits are attributed to the partners directly. Complete the employer registration with the CCSS if already performed, and notify the chosen Luxembourg credit institution to activate the operational bank account.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement)
Completed VAT registration application via MyGuichet
Partnership agreement extract confirming fiscal transparency
Identity documents and residence permits of partners and manager
Bank account reference (IBAN) for the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT or ACD issues a request for further information (e.g., projected turnover, partner domicile, or transparency clarification), respond within the 30-day statutory notice period with the partnership agreement and RCS publication; if the tax office proposes to treat the SCSp as taxable, an administrative complaint or timely corrective declaration can restate its pass-through status; VAT registration is effective retroactively from the RCS registration date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie et de la compétitivité (Direction de l'industrie); Administration de l'environnement for environmental matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) granted under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to and exercise of crafts, activities and trades; the SCSp also requires commune-level occupancy authorization for the studio premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (National Environment Agency), Department of Environmental Approvals and Waste Management.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 4 establishment under the Grand-Ducal regulations implementing the Law of 24 May 2000 on the communal regime (commercial building and studio without dangerous substances) — subject only to a prior declaration ('notification') to the municipality; a full EIA study under the Law of 15 May 2018 is not required, and no environmental operating permit ('autorisation d'exploitation') is triggered for a dry digital post-production activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the municipal wastewater discharge rules (sanitary waters only; no industrial effluent given the fully digital workflow); technical plant noise limited to 35 dB(A) at night and 45 dB(A) by day at the nearest sensitive receptor; all electronic equipment, GPU servers and audio hardware managed under the EU WEEE regime through Administration de l'environnement-approved take-back schemes; HVAC systems must use non-VOC refrigerants per Regulation (EU) No 517/2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CGDIS (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours) fire-safety survey and clearance for the commune's occupancy permit, including alarm and extinguisher compliance; structural engineer's certificate confirming floor load capacity for server racks (minimum 7.5 kN/m²); electrical installation certification; and workplace clearance from the Inspection du travail et des Mines (ITM) covering ergonomic screen workstations, hearing protection in audio booths, and electrical safety under the Luxembourg Labor Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue for direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD). Luxembourg VAT and registration duties authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT). Central business administration portal: guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SCSp in Luxembourg must first obtain a Luxembourg business registration number (RCS number) via the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (LBR). For tax purposes, the SCSp must then apply to the ACD for a Luxembourg identification number (matricule) covering direct tax obligations and register for VAT status where applicable with the AEDT using the VAT registration form (formulaire 640). Non-established taxable persons may be required to appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative if they have no fixed establishment in Luxembourg, unless an exemption applies under EU VAT rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, meaning Luxembourg does not impose corporate income tax at the partnership level; partners are taxed on their respective shares of income. Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election, but partnerships may apply for VAT grouping under Luxembourg VAT rules and may structure profit-sharing to alter the attribution of Luxembourg-source income, subject to anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD and the Luxembourg anti-abuse rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for established Luxembourg small businesses; non-established foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg are generally required to register for VAT irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose a universal real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. E-invoicing is accepted and PEPPOL-compliant formats are supported. Submission of VAT returns and recapitulative statements is performed electronically through the AEDT portal. No API-based real-time pre-clearance of invoices is currently mandated for standard B2B services, including subtitle and AI services. Taxable persons must issue invoices in compliance with Luxembourg invoicing rules and retain SAF-T-compatible records for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exports is available for goods dispatched or transported outside the EU provided the supplier retains proof of export and receives a valid EU customer number. For cross-border B2B services, including automated subtitle and AI voice services, the place of supply is normally the country where the business customer is established; the supply is therefore outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and zero-rated from a Luxembourg perspective. The supplier must obtain the customer's valid VAT identification number and maintain contemporaneous evidence of the commercial transaction and delivery of digital work.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) or electronic export declaration validated by Luxembourg customs
Bill of Lading or other transport documentation evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence showing settlement of the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT administration may retrospectively deny zero-rating where the documentary evidence is insufficient, leading to reassessment of Luxembourg VAT at the standard 17% rate plus default interest. Fraudulent or knowingly incorrect zero-rating claims can attract penalties of up to EUR 25,000 per offense or, in serious cases, tax fraud charges carrying fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for responsible officers. Directors and tax representatives of the SCSp may incur joint liability for VAT clawed back from a failed zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); foreign-exchange and cross-border payment statistics are reported to the BCL, while credit institutions and payment institutions are supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg has no separate foreign-exchange administration; the Ministry of Finance is responsible for sanctions and exchange-control policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility applies under Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-65 and EMU rules. The euro is freely convertible both internally and vis-à-vis foreign currencies; no Luxembourg restrictions exist on opening foreign-currency accounts, entering FX transactions, or remitting profits/distributions. SCSp distributions to non-resident partners are not subject to exchange-control licensing; applicable hurdles are fiscal only (anti-abuse, withholding tax on certain payments, transfer-pricing documentation, substance requirements) and AML/KYC onboarding requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no export-proceeds repatriation, surrender, or mandatory conversion requirement. AI subtitle/licensing receipts received in USD or third currencies may be retained in the SCSp's foreign-currency accounts; for Luxembourg statutory accounts they must be translated into EUR under applicable accounting standards. Such receipts remain subject to normal tax declaration, VAT treatment for cross-border digital services where applicable, and anti-money-laundering transaction justification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (central treasury), with separate Foreign-Currency Sub-Accounts for USD/EUR collections and settlement

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account for domestic payroll, tax and invoice payments
Operational Account and Commercial LC/SBLC issuance desk
Operational Account and cross-currency liquidity/swaps execution account
Operational Account and multi-currency treasury overlay
Operational Account and e-commerce collection settlement via payment service providers

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail, low as a substitute for a regulated credit institution. EU/EEA-licensed EMIs and payment institutions (Wise, Stripe, Payoneer, Multitude) can legally passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and provide EUR/foreign-currency virtual IBANs, cross-border FX conversion, card acquiring, and faster settlement for the AI subtitle marketplace. They are not 'banks' for escrow, depositor protection, commercial loans, or documentary credits; funds held with EMIs are not protected by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme in the same manner. Offshore/non-EEA EMIs that have not passported cannot lawfully provide payment services to the SCSp in Luxembourg; use of such EMIs triggers CSSF regulatory exposure and bank KYC concerns. Optimal blueprint: use an EMI only for micro-transactions and marketplace pay-ins below 15% of monthly turnover, with all capital injections, profit repatriation, tax payments, and large trade settlements through BCL-supervised banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not imposed by Luxembourg statute for all cases, but Luxembourg banks generally apply internal de-risking requiring the authorised manager/general partner and every 10%+ ultimate beneficial owner to complete either an in-person interview in Luxembourg or a notarised video-identification process with apostilled/certified documents. For an SCSp with a foreign corporate general partner and no Luxembourg director, the expectation is a physical or high-tier video interview before account opening; non-resident politically exposed persons and partners from non-EEA jurisdictions face stricter mandates. Remote opening is feasible for EEA-resident individuals/corporations complying with the AML Law of 19 February 2021 (identification, source-of-funds, source-of-wealth).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is a stateless-looking partnership with no employees, no office, and a corporate general partner formed in an offshore/low-tax jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft constitutive deed and the published RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) declaration; organisational chart with all UBOs; business plan for AI dubbing/post-production studio; lease or licensed co-working address in Luxembourg; minutes appointing authorised signatories; proof of operational substance (bank account, VAT file, payroll or subcontracting agreements, equipment licences).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity contributions originate from non-EEA private investors without matching transaction narrative or are received from third-party accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital contribution/subscription resolutions; bank-to-bank statements showing source account; source-of-wealth for each investor (tax returns, share sale agreements, dividend vouchers, inheritance documents); latest audited/certified financials of investor; EUR valuation of in-kind contributions; SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI and SCSp name/LEI in remittance information.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume invoice flows from multiple international content platforms (Stripe/Wise, Netflix, YouTube, AI voice vendors) with abstract service descriptions such as 'licence fee' or 'subtitle services'
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Framework agreements, sales orders and purchase orders; detailed per-invoice statements mapping copyright/royalty cessions to specific motion-picture titles; metadata logs showing subtitle/AI voice tasks, video fingerprints, and deliverables; KYC of main trade counterparties; VAT treatment analysis (reverse charge vs deemed taxable in Luxembourg); transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through distribution to foreign partners soon after receipts might indicate bulk cash-out or tax evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership agreement clauses on profit-sharing and cash management; board/management resolutions approving distributions; annual statutory reports proving distributable reserves; current/future tax provisions and Luxembourg tax advice confirming transparency as a partnership; FATCA/CRS classification and partner-by-partner UBO/entity details; bank account statements showing historic revenue and operating expense flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a newly created SCSp to receive cross-border funds within 90 days of incorporation, with no credit history or audited financials
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Incorporation deed and RBE registration certificate; notarised/government-certified corporate documents (Certificate of Non-Bankruptcy, Certificate of Good Standing) for all partners; LEI number and CSSF/financial sector registration (if not exempt); detailed treasury forecast (cash flow budget, expected inflows/outflows); commercial contracts and counterparty due diligence; reference letters from service providers; bank internal risk-scoring submission prepared by counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use only a regulated Luxembourg credit institution account. For EEA investors prefer SEPA Credit Transfer (IBAN LU + BIC) with remittance narrative 'Capital contribution - [SCSp legal name] - [LEI]'; for non-EEA investors use SWIFT MT103 with ISO/Harmonised purpose code EQUI (equity injection), bank confirmation of funds, and KYC package attached. Before any injection, file or update the Luxembourg RBE and execute capital call/capital contribution minutes; the bank will verify consistency with the constitutional deed and partnership accounting. For convertible loans or shareholder loans, use purpose code LOAN or INTC (intercompany loan) and provide executed loan agreement, pricing/interest-rate policy, and source-of-funds documentation; commercial reasonableness and transfer-pricing documentation are required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 for high-value non-EEA counterparties (EUR, USD, GBP); field 70 must contain invoice/PO number and service description, with purpose code INVC for trade invoices. For EEA vendors/royalty partners: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer up to settlement limits, using debtor and creditor IBANs. For large studio-equipment acquisitions and content licensing where the vendor requires shipment/acceptance security: irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit via the Luxembourg bank (UCP 600), plus Incoterms-compliant transport/proof-of-delivery documents and TARGET2/COR1 payment completion. All outbound payments must pass sanctions screening, FATF/CFT rules, and Luxembourg VAT cash-management: reverse-charge intra-EU B2B services must be declared and paid through AED, while non-EU royalty outflows may be subject to Luxembourg withholding/beneficial-owner tests before payment is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards (up to 12-24 months) executed under an ISDA 2002/FX Master Agreement with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution
EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF and EUR/JPY deliverable forwards for subtitle/localisation invoices denominated in major non-EUR currencies
Cross-currency swaps (EURUSD and EURGBP) to align long-term AI licensing receivables with EUR operating costs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for restricted or low-liquidity currencies used in payments from markets with exchange controls, settled in EUR or another clearing-eligible currency
Plain-vanilla FX options, zero-cost collars and participating forwards for cash-flow protection; exotic options are not permissible without separate board approval

FX swaps for short-term EUR liquidity management and rollover of cross-currency settlement balances, subject to EMIR reporting and variation margin (IM/VM) obligations if the counterparty exceeds clearing thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels) – Luxembourg GAAP financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year end; if approval of general meeting is later, within 1 month of approval (mandatory electronic filing through the e-Justice / RCS platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €750 per contravention; penalty interest; risk of judicial strike-off if filing overdue for 2 consecutive financial years; publication of the decision is possible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Registre des Bénéficiaires Efficaces RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Beneficial Ownership Registry (RBE – Registre des Bénéficiaires Efficaces)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of initial RBE registration, plus 30 days; any change in beneficial ownership or partnership interest transfer must be filed within 30 days of the occurrence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to €1,250,000 and imprisonment (for corporate representatives); administrative penalties for late or incorrect confirmation; publication of non-compliance may be ordered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return (Déclaration de l’impôt sur les sociétés et de l’impôt commercial communal) – informational filing for fiscally transparent undertakings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year fiscal period: due by 31 December of the following year (electronic filing); if paper filed, by 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to 10% of assessed tax (if any) plus statutory interest of 0.6% per month; possibility of ex officio assessment and additional tax surcharge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return and EU Sales Listing (only if VAT registered, typical for active commercial activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Enregistrement et Domaines (AED – Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns depend on annual turnover; annual recapitulative EU sales statement due by 31 January of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 10% of the VAT due, statutory interest of 0.6% per month, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent declarations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit required if the SCSp exceeds two of the following three thresholds (per Luxembourg law of 23 September 2016): total balance sheet €4.4 million; net turnover €8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. For small undertakings (under these thresholds), the general partners may be exempt, but the articles of association or a minority of partners may still require an audit. Additionally, if the SCSp qualifies as an investment fund (common operating context), an independent audit may be required by CSSF regulations if the entity manages assets over a certain volume.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (based on Commercial Code and annual accounts law) is the default; IFRS is permitted as an alternative for financial reporting. The SCSp must maintain books and records in compliance with the 10th Directive and Luxembourg accounting law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, within 30 days of the anniversary of the SCSp's initial RBE registration, an annual confirmation of beneficial ownership must be filed with the Luxembourg RBE. Any shareholding or partnership interest transfer affecting the beneficial owner list must be reported within 30 days. The register of partners (registered list) must be updated permanently and mirrored by an internal beneficial ownership register. No additional tax filing is required for the annual confirmation, but the data must be consistent with the annual accounts and tax return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members/partners (list of limited and general partners with capital contributions)
Minute book (shareholders'/partners' meetings and managers' resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 2,200 per year (typical annual fee for a professional Luxembourg registered office / agent for a SCSp)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 per year (only applicable if audit threshold exceeded or requested by partners; typical for a small-to-medium SCSp with revenue below €8.8 million)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate corporate income tax (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 1.19% + municipal business tax avg 6.75%) for taxable companies; 0% for SCSp as a tax-transparent pass-through entity unless opt-in under Luxembourg corporate law
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for dividends and capital gains; 80% deduction for qualifying IP income (IP Box); notional interest deduction for equity-financed investments; double-dip hybrid mismatch restrictions apply under ATAD

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 500 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu collectif) filed electronically through the eCDF portal (espace professionnel)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Paper filing by 31 May following the calendar fiscal year-end; electronic filing extension to 31 December of the same year (additional administrative extension possible on request)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, commercial registry number (RCS), tax number (TVA/RC), and registered office of the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name, country of tax residence, and foreign tax identification number; attach valid tax residence certificate (TRC) for treaty claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Net Taxable Profit or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed total net income from all sources before profit allocation, calculated in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP adjusted for tax depreciation and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report their allocable share of Luxembourg-source income in their domestic returns; the SCSp files this information on behalf of all partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Allocation to General and Limited Partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net taxable income/losses among partners according to the partnership agreement (SCSp is tax-transparent, thus no partnership-level tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each partner's pro-rata share must be disclosed separately; non-resident partners are not taxed in Luxembourg on purely business income unless attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Tax Credits and Advance Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for foreign-tax credit, investment tax credit, and withholding tax credits arising from Luxembourg-source dividends or royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may credit underlying foreign taxes if eligible under DTA; submit DTA relief application together with TRC before the filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty up to EUR 1,250 per return; additional 0.6% per month late-payment interest on assessed tax; systematic default may lead to tax reassessment by the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (ACD) and criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions by SCSp to partners because the vehicle is tax-transparent; if the SCSp voluntarily elects Luxembourg corporate taxation, standard dividend WHT is 15% (reduced to 5% for substantial shareholdings and 0% under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on any residual Luxembourg-source payments (e.g., interest if the SCSp becomes corporately taxed), the taxpayer must (i) hold a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the treaty partner, (ii) complete the Luxembourg administrative claim form (ATR clearance), and (iii) file the request through the eCDF portal or by registered letter to the RTS (Renseignements et Transferts Sommaires) division of the ACD. For treaty-reduced withholding, the paying agent must receive the TRC before the payment date; retroactive reclaim requires a separate refund application with supporting legal entity ownership documentation and proof of substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound royalties and interest is 0% in Luxembourg (neither tax withheld nor collectible); no reduction under treaties is required as domestic law already exempts these payments from withholding. However, anti-hybrid rules may disallow deductions if the payee is a tax-transparent entity or if the payment is deductible in Luxembourg and not taxed in the recipient jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No specific local monetary threshold for Master/Local File in Luxembourg; OECD transfer pricing principles are applied. Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) is mandatory for multinational groups (including SCSp chain) with consolidated annual revenue exceeding EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) register as in other EU-adjacent jurisdictions, but the ACD applies a robust substance-over-form doctrine rooted in ATAD, the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive, and the OECD BEPS Minimum Standards. For an SCSp, economic substance is required to validate treaty residence, any tax-exempt income claim, and to avoid classification as a transparent shell. Evidence includes premises, staff, commencement of activity, real decision-making in Luxembourg, and adequate capitalisation vis-à-vis risk assumptions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting partnership income, inflating deductible expenses, falsifying partner allocation ratios, or making fictitious distributions to non-resident shell partners for tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of all underpaid taxes plus a surcharge of 10%–50% of the evaded amount; administrative fine up to EUR 125,000; imprisonment up to 1 year for wilful evasion under Article 110 LGBTQI+ (Luxembourg Income Tax Act).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners face personal, joint and several liability for corporate tax debts if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution orders, asset seizures, travel bans (Courts of Luxembourg) and criminal incarceration up to 2 years for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a pass-through conduit without any real economic activity, without personnel, premises or risk management, and in a purely circular treaty-shopping arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under national anti-abuse provisions, the tax administration may disregard the SCSp's existence, deny treaty benefits, re-assess income and withholding obligations on a look-through basis, and apply a 5%–20% penalty on the revised tax liability; potential revocation of corporate benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for taxes arising from re-characterised transactions, subject to clawback of distributed profits, travel bans, and imprisonment where a knowing sham is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Beneficial Ownership Failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a beneficial ownership register (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) for the SCSp, or concealing the identity of beneficial partners behind nominee chains or bearer structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg AML law (law of 12 November 2004 and subsequent amendments): fines up to EUR 250,000 for legal entities; additional €5,000 per week of non-corrected breach; criminal sanctions include prison time up to 5 years for money laundering. The Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) enforces mandatory filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorised managers are personally obligated to identify beneficial owners; failure leads to personal fines, revocation of permits, prohibition from holding management functions, civil damages to third parties, and in severe cases imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit Master File/Local File documentation upon request of the ACD, or disregard of arm's length pricing on intra-SCSp transactions (e.g., subcontracting to AI voice-cloning service providers).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may estimate taxable income using best available information, apply a penalty of 5%–10% of the under-declared profit, and impose a specific penalty up to EUR 100,000 for serious non-cooperation; interest on late adjustments continues to accrue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incomplete transfer pricing documentation or knowingly certify incorrect pricing are subject to fines up to 25% of the tax deficiency, disqualification as directors in Luxembourg, and criminal liability for aiding tax evasion if proven intentional.
